name: SWE-Gym
size: 2,438 train instances from 11 Python repos (HF split count)
summary: Real GitHub issue tasks with FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests, built for training and verifying SWE agents. Lite (230) and Raw (64,689 unvalidated PR rows) variants exist.
how_to_use: Use as a small, clean RL pool with per-repo Docker images from the SWE-Gym repo; pair with the SWE-bench test harness as verifier. Combine with larger sets for scale.
caveats: Small. Only 2.4k tasks, so pass-rate filtering leaves little. Repo overlap with SWE-bench test repos is a known contamination concern for SWE-bench evals. Images must be built or pulled separately.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("SWE-Gym/SWE-Gym", split="train")

name: SWE-smith
summary: Synthetic bug-injection tasks generated per repo (LM-written, rewritten, procedural and PR-mirror bugs) with test-based validation and per-task Docker image names. Java and other-language variants are listed under SWE-bench on HF.
how_to_use: Large cheap source of verifiable SWE tasks. Filter by pass rate of your current policy before RL; use the image_name column to pull per-task containers.
caveats: Synthetic bugs are easier and less natural than real issues; problem statements are LM generated. Nemotron-Cascade used it as one of five sources, not alone. Check test-leak risk: FAIL_TO_PASS tests are present in the repo image.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("SWE-bench/SWE-smith", split="train")

name: SWE-rebench (nebius, v1)
summary: Continuously mined Python GitHub issue tasks with install configs, F2P/P2P tests and docker_image names, from Nebius; also feeds a decontaminated leaderboard.
how_to_use: Use the filtered split for quality; docker_image/install_config let you reproduce environments. Good RL pool next to SWE-Gym and R2E-Gym.
caveats: The huge test split is unfiltered: some tasks have ambiguous statements or weak tests. Underlying repo licenses vary (license_name column). Check time overlap with your eval set.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("nebius/SWE-rebench", split="filtered")

name: SWE-rebench V2
summary: Language-agnostic executable SWE tasks with pre-built images, F2P/P2P tests and LLM quality filtering. A companion set has 126,300 PR-derived tasks.
how_to_use: Best open multilingual SWE RL pool as of late 2026. Start with the issue-linked set, add the PRs set for volume after filtering.
caveats: PR-derived tasks lack issue text quality guarantees. Images are large. Repo licenses vary (license column). Leaderboard maintained for V1 Python only per HF discussion.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("nebius/SWE-rebench-V2", split="train")

name: R2E-Gym (Subset)
summary: Procedurally generated executable environments from commits (back-translated issue text, LM-generated tests) used to train SWE agents and verifiers; includes dev splits in the Lite variant.
how_to_use: Use as a second RL source beside real-issue sets; pull images named in docker_image.
caveats: Problem statements are back-translated, tests partly LM-written, so label noise exists. Code repo last pushed 2025-07-13. The Lite variant card has no license field.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("R2E-Gym/R2E-Gym-Subset", split="train")

name: SWE-bench-extra
summary: Nebius earlier large SWE-bench-format task collection (patch, test_patch, F2P/P2P, license per instance), precursor to SWE-rebench.
how_to_use: Mostly superseded by SWE-rebench; still usable for SFT or RL if you build the environments yourself.
caveats: No image columns, so environments must be reconstructed. Superseded by SWE-rebench.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("nebius/SWE-bench-extra", split="train")

name: SWE-bench (full, train/test splits)
license: MIT (GitHub repo; HF card has no license field)
size: 2,294 test + 225 dev instances in the HF repo; no train split listed
summary: The original 2,294-issue benchmark, now with eval_script, image and log_parser columns. A SWE-bench-Train subset (1,063 questions per the Nemotron-Cascade card) was used by Nemotron-Cascade.
how_to_use: Treat as eval, not training. If using the old train data, exclude repos in your eval set as Nemotron-Cascade did.
caveats: The HF repo currently exposes test/dev only (verified 2026-11-24). Train data cited by Nemotron-Cascade came from princeton-nlp/SWE-bench; repo overlap contaminates Verified/Lite evals. Git history leak was patched upstream (PR 471).
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("SWE-bench/SWE-bench", split="test")

name: SWE-bench-Live
size: 1,000 test, 1,888 full, 300 lite, 500 verified instances (split counts)
summary: Continuously updated issue-resolution benchmark with docker_image, test_cmds and rebuild_cmds per task, intended to stay ahead of contamination.
how_to_use: Use older monthly slices as extra RL data only if you keep recent months held out.
caveats: Designed as eval; training on it burns the contamination guarantee. Split definitions may change between updates.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("SWE-bench-Live/SWE-bench-Live", split="full")

name: Multi-SWE-RL
size: Community RL dataset, first batch data_20240601_20250331; per-language counts not machine-readable on the card
summary: ByteDance Seed community effort to collect multilingual SWE RL instances (unannotated new instances plus discarded Multi-SWE-bench instances).
how_to_use: Treat as raw material: you must build environments with the multi-swe-bench toolkit before using it for RL.
caveats: Unannotated and license is vague ('other'). Last HF update 2025-07-23. Little documentation of sizes in the card, so size is not verified.

name: SWE-Dev
summary: Feature-driven development tasks: product requirement, partial source, developer-written unit tests and ground-truth code, supporting SFT and RL with test-based reward.
how_to_use: Use for feature implementation (not bug fixing) RL, executing the bundled unit tests as reward.
caveats: Exact train/test counts not verified here. A separate zai-org/SWE-Dev-train holds SFT/RFT trajectories (17,871 sft, 2,276 rft rows) with no license on its card. GitHub code repo has no license.

name: SWE-Synth
license: none stated on dataset card (null in API)
summary: Synthetic bug-fix instances with setup patches, F2P/P2P tests and problem statements, plus Moatless SFT trajectories in sibling datasets.
how_to_use: Use as additional synthetic SWE data after checking license with authors.
caveats: No license on card, so redistribution rights unclear. Last updated 2025-03.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("swesynth/SWE-Synth", split="train")

name: SWE-Flow / Repo2RLEnv swe_flow recipe
size: SWE-Flow code; Repo2RLEnv sample set FineEnvs/repo2rlenv-swe-flow has 100 Harbor tasks
summary: Test-driven synthesis: trace passing tests, remove exercised functions, ask the agent to reconstruct them, reward via retained tests. Hugging Face Repo2RLEnv now packages the recipe as Harbor tasks.
how_to_use: Use Repo2RLEnv to turn your own repos into Harbor-format RL tasks.
caveats: Sample HF set is only 100 tasks with mixed source licenses. SWE-Flow repo last pushed 2025-06-29 with 40 stars.

name: Repo2RLEnv
summary: Hugging Face tool that turns any repository into verifiable RL environments for coding agents in Harbor task format (instruction, Dockerfile, tests, reward script).
how_to_use: Use to build private RL tasks from your own codebases with the same format as Terminal-Bench 2.
caveats: Young project; recipe quality varies. Verify tests cannot be edited by the agent in each generated task.

name: OpenSWE (GAIR, daVinci-Env)
license: other (gated, access conditions on card); code repo licensed per GitHub as NOASSERTION; search snippet says AGPL-3.0 (unverified)
size: 10K-100K rows (HF size category); paper claims 45,320 Docker environments
summary: Large open set of executable Python SWE environments with synthesis pipeline released.
how_to_use: Request access, read license terms, then use for large-scale RL after pass-rate filtering.
caveats: Gated with auto-approval; license ambiguous. Counts from paper abstract via search, not confirmed from API.

name: Lego-RL-2699 and LegoFlow-SWE
size: 1K-10K Harbor RL environments (HF size category); Verified-500 packaged as Harbor tasks
summary: SWE-Lego family: Harbor-format RL environments, teacher trajectories and a Harbor-packaged SWE-bench Verified for evaluating against the same trainer.
how_to_use: Use if your trainer reads Harbor tasks; check AGPL implications before redistributing derived data.
caveats: AGPL-3.0 on RL set is restrictive. LEGO-RL paper id seen in card (2608.17393) not independently opened. SWE-Lego code repo Apache-2.0.

name: Nemotron-Cascade-RL-SWE
size: Per card (16K-prompt slice): 23,236 SWE-Fixer, 2,472 SWE-Smith (card prints '24,72'), 1,063 SWE-Bench-Train, 4,244 SWE-rebench questions
summary: NVIDIA recipe data for SWE RL: difficulty-filtered mix of SWE-Bench-Train, SWE-rebench, SWE-smith, R2E-Gym-Subset and SWE-Fixer, with repos from SWE-bench Verified excluded to avoid contamination.
how_to_use: Take as a template for mixing five sources and excluding eval repos. Reward there is execution-free (reward model), not Docker.
caveats: Card states no Docker execution reward was used, so this is not an execution-verified recipe. Question counts are on the card; the SWE-Smith figure is garbled on the card.

name: NVIDIA SWE-Zero / SWE-Hero OpenHands trajectories
summary: OpenHands agent trajectories with model_patch and repo license columns, for SFT or rejection sampling on SWE tasks.
how_to_use: Filter by resolved status and license column before SFT.
caveats: Resolve labels are not in the verified column list (instance_id, repo, license, trajectory_id, trajectory, model_patch, dataset). Teacher-model terms apply; check card.

name: DeepCoder-Preview-Dataset
size: 24K problems with tests per card; configs lcbv5 (599 train, 279 test) and codeforces (408 test) verified in API
summary: Verified-test competitive programming set used to train DeepCoder-14B: TACO verified, PrimeIntellect SYNTHETIC-1 code and LiveCodeBench problems with test lists.
how_to_use: Standard small RL pool for GRPO code runs; run tests with a sandbox (SandboxFusion, verl's code reward).
caveats: Includes LiveCodeBench v5 train problems, so do not eval on lcbv5 train/test overlap. Only 2 of the configs inspected; 24K figure from card.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("agentica-org/DeepCoder-Preview-Dataset", "lcbv5", split="train")

name: open-r1/codeforces
size: 10,024 problems (9,556 train + 468 test); verifiable config 8,338 train + 422 test
summary: Codeforces problems with statements, editorials, official tests and generated checkers, including interactive problems; the 'verifiable' config keeps problems with complete tests.
how_to_use: Use the verifiable config for RL; run C++/Python with checker support. Problems carry a rating column for difficulty filtering.
caveats: Needs a judge that handles special checkers and interactors. Statements are scraped from codeforces.com (card gives CC-BY-4.0; rights to original content not verified).
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("open-r1/codeforces", "verifiable", split="train")

name: CodeContests (DeepMind)
summary: Competitive problems from Codeforces, CodeChef, AtCoder and others with generated tests and correct/incorrect human solutions in Python, C++ and Java.
how_to_use: Classic source of RL problems; many prepared versions exist (Eurus-2, Nemotron-RL).
caveats: False-positive rate of original generated tests is high; CodeContests+ and CodeContests-O exist to fix this. Python 2 solutions present.

name: TACO
summary: Large algorithmic problem set with tests, solutions, difficulty and algorithm tags, aggregated from many contest sites.
how_to_use: Use difficulty/skill tags for curriculum; filter via the verified subset in DeepCoder-Preview-Dataset.
caveats: Raw test quality varies (DeepCoder filtered to a verified subset). Upstream site terms not fully clear.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("BAAI/TACO", "ALL", split="train")

name: APPS
summary: Interview-level and competition Python problems with solutions and test cases.
how_to_use: Old but common RL sanity set; heavily contaminated in modern pretraining data.
caveats: Known noisy tests and duplicates. Prefer cleaned derivatives.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("codeparrot/apps", split="train")

name: CodeContests+
summary: CodeContests with LLM-generated, validated test generators and checkers to raise test quality, built using SandboxFusion; intended as better RL verifiers.
how_to_use: Prefer over raw CodeContests for RL reward accuracy.
caveats: Larger test multiplicities cost more sandbox time. Sandbox required.

name: CodeContests-O
license: not stated in card header (API license null); check card
size: 11,407 train + 162 test + 114 valid problems; dataset_size about 714 GB
summary: Feedback-driven iterative test case generation for CodeContests problems: generators, checkers and corner cases.
how_to_use: Use the generators rather than download the whole set; partial download by file.
caveats: Enormous (about 325 GB download). License unspecified. Paper arXiv 2601.13682.

name: Skywork-OR1-RL-Data
license: Apache-2.0 on GitHub repo; HF card has no license field
summary: RL-ready math and code problems in verl format (prompt, reward_model.ground_truth) with per-model pass difficulty labels for 1.5B, 7B and 32B R1 distills.
how_to_use: Use extra_info.model_difficulty to drop always-solved and never-solved items before GRPO.
caveats: Card license missing. Code ground truth are large test blobs (about 1.5 GB for 14k code rows).
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("Skywork/Skywork-OR1-RL-Data", split="code")

name: SYNTHETIC-1
size: 1,994,262 rows; card sections: 777k math, 144k algorithmic coding, 70k SWE, 61k code understanding
summary: Prime Intellect crowdsourced DeepSeek-R1 traces with verification_info and score columns across math, coding, SWE and more.
how_to_use: Filter by score and task_type for verified-correct traces or reuse problems with verification_info for RL.
caveats: R1-generated; check DeepSeek license terms. Wide mix, many non-code rows.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("PrimeIntellect/SYNTHETIC-1", split="train")

name: Eurus-2-RL-Data
summary: PRIME RL training set: outcome-verifiable math answers and coding test cases from APPS, CodeContests, TACO and Codeforces, deduplicated.
how_to_use: Early baseline mix for outcome-reward RL.
caveats: Cleaning was mostly deduplication, so test quality is raw.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("PRIME-RL/Eurus-2-RL-Data", split="train")

name: Nemotron-RL-coding-competitive_coding
license: CC-BY-SA-4.0 in card metadata, card text says CC-BY-4.0 (inconsistent)
size: 16,083 train rows in metadata; card text says 25k records, 7.62 GB
summary: NeMo Gym RLVR set of Python competitive problems with unit tests from CodeContests and open-r1/codeforces.
how_to_use: Use with NeMo Gym or convert to verl format.
caveats: License inconsistency and count mismatch between YAML and prose; confirm before redistribution. Tests are inlined, so about 5 GB.

name: KodCode-V1
summary: Fully synthetic coding questions with solutions and pytest-style tests validated by execution; fields include gpt pass percentage and difficulty.
how_to_use: Use gpt_pass_percentage and gpt_difficulty to select medium difficulty for RL; tests are runnable.
caveats: Non-commercial license. Generated with GPT-4 family so OpenAI terms may apply. Easier than competition sets.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("KodCode/KodCode-V1", split="train")

name: rStar-Coder
summary: Competitive problems with mutually verified test cases, with configs synthetic_sft, synthetic_rl, synthetic_rl_testcase, seed_sft, seed_testcase.
how_to_use: Use synthetic_rl plus synthetic_rl_testcase for RL; seed_* configs have real problems.
caveats: Test cases live in separate config, join by id. Large. Solutions from Qwen/DeepSeek models.

name: OpenCodeReasoning
summary: R1-generated reasoning solutions for competitive problems with difficulty column and source license column.
how_to_use: Use for SFT warm start before RL; join split_1 to original problems by index.
caveats: split_1 lacks question text and needs reconstruction from source datasets.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("nvidia/OpenCodeReasoning", "split_0", split="split_0")

name: LiveCodeBench
size: 980 stars; problem releases dated by contest
summary: Contamination-aware benchmark from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces with problem release dates; DeepCoder used the lcbv5 train problems for RL.
how_to_use: Use date filtering to keep eval clean of your RL data.
caveats: Repo last pushed 2025-07-16. Training on recent problems makes it unusable as eval.

name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
size: under 1K tasks (HF size category); read-only mirror
summary: Hard terminal tasks in Harbor format (instruction, Docker environment, tests); official leaderboard at tbench.ai. Also terminal-bench 2.1, 3.0 and a science split on HF.
how_to_use: Run with Harbor; use as eval, and use Harbor task format to author RL tasks.
caveats: Few tasks so not an RL pool; HF page is a mirror, primary repo is GitHub. Unofficial leaderboard warning on card.

name: Spider
summary: Cross-domain text-to-SQL; databases are executable SQLite so execution accuracy gives a reward.
how_to_use: Train GRPO with execution-match reward on SQLite, compare result sets.
caveats: Saturated for strong models; the HF dataset has questions and gold SQL but SQLite databases come from the Spider site or a separate dataset.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("xlangai/spider", "spider", split="train")

name: BIRD mini-dev and BIRD-Critic
size: bird_mini_dev (1K-10K rows by size category); BIRD-Critic SQLite also on HF
summary: Harder, more realistic text-to-SQL with execution-based evaluation; BIRD-Critic covers SQL debugging with test cases.
how_to_use: Use BIRD train (birdsql/bird23-train-filtered) for execution-reward RL; mini-dev for eval.
caveats: Exact row counts not read here. BIRD train is older and sometimes noisy. Execution match can be gamed by empty or equivalent result sets.

name: Lean Workbook
summary: Auto-formalized competition-style problems in Lean 4, used for theorem-prover RL; Goedel-LM/Lean-workbook-proofs has 29,750 proofs.
how_to_use: Verifier is the Lean 4 compiler (kimina-lean-server, Lean REPL); filter by pass rate.
caveats: Auto-formalization noise: some statements trivial or false. Compiler checks proof validity only, not statement faithfulness.

name: Kimina-Prover-Promptset
summary: Lean 4 formal statements with natural-language versions used for Kimina-Prover RL.
how_to_use: Pair with kimina-lean-server as verifier.
caveats: No license on card. Project repo MIT for the server.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("project-numina/Kimina-Prover-Promptset", split="train")

name: NuminaMath-LEAN
summary: Competition problems with formal statements, ground-truth proofs and an rl_data field for Lean 4 training.
how_to_use: Use formal_statement with a Lean verifier; check rl_data to choose RL subsets.
caveats: Not every row has a verified proof; the field semantics should be read from the card.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("AI-MO/NuminaMath-LEAN", split="train")

name: FormalMATH
summary: Large Lean 4 formal math benchmark spanning olympiad to undergraduate level.
how_to_use: Mainly an eval; subsets could feed RL if decontaminated.
caveats: Row count not read from the API response. Eval use.

name: DeepSeek-ProverBench
summary: Held-out Lean 4 problems for DeepSeek-Prover-V2; related V1 training data deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Prover-V1 has license 'other'.
how_to_use: Eval only.
caveats: License field absent; DeepSeek-Prover-V1 data license is 'other' (see card).

name: Verina
summary: Verifiable code generation in Lean: each task has description, Lean code, signature, tests and rejected inputs; evaluates code, spec and proof generation. VerinaLite/Plus variants exist.
how_to_use: Good for training models to write code plus specs plus proofs, with Lean checker as verifier.
caveats: Tiny (189 tasks). Treat as eval or few-shot.
load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("sunblaze-ucb/verina", split="train")

name: CLEVER
summary: Lean benchmark for end-to-end verified code generation: specification and implementation proven correct.
how_to_use: Use as eval or hard RL seed.
caveats: Small benchmark. Dataset ids on HF not verified so only GitHub listed.

name: Reasoning Gym
summary: Library of procedurally generated reasoning tasks with programmatic verifiers, including code and algorithm tasks; infinite data.
how_to_use: Use for generic verifiable RL and curriculum via its difficulty settings; NVIDIA published a Nemotron-RL-ReasoningGym dataset.
caveats: Not mostly code; coverage of real programming is limited.

name: verifiers (Prime Intellect)
summary: Library for RL environments and evals; environments are installable packages and can be published to the Prime Intellect Environments Hub.
how_to_use: Write a reward function plus dataset as an environment, then train with prime-rl or other trainers.
caveats: API changes quickly. Hub environments are community made with light review.

name: OpenEnv
summary: Interface library for RL post-training with environments (Gym-style API served over containers).
how_to_use: Wrap code execution tasks as containerized envs to plug into TRL or other trainers.
caveats: Repo moved under the openenv org; early API.

name: NVIDIA NeMo Gym
summary: Framework and collection of RLVR environments and datasets (competitive coding, SWE) for NeMo-RL and other trainers.
how_to_use: Use its datasets (Nemotron-RL-*) and verifier servers with NeMo-RL.
caveats: Dataset licenses vary per dataset.

name: Harbor
summary: Framework for running agents in containerized tasks: used for Terminal-Bench 2, SWE-bench adapters, and RL rollouts; supports Docker and cloud sandboxes.
how_to_use: Use as the harness to run tasks in parallel and collect reward from test.sh output.
caveats: Repo renamed from laude-institute/harbor; old URL redirects.

name: verl
summary: HybridFlow RL post-training framework; supports GRPO/PPO with rule-based and sandbox code rewards. Verified active on GitHub API.
how_to_use: Pick based on scale and ecosystem; write or plug a code-execution reward that calls a sandbox (SandboxFusion, Harbor, Docker).
caveats: Feature claims reflect repo description only; check docs for exact code-reward support. Stars and push date as of 2026-11-24.
